**(a)** Write down the equation of the horizontal asymptote. **[1]**

Show that $a^{x}=e^{x\ln a}$ for $a>0$, and hence write $5^{x}$ in the form $e^{kx}$.
markscheme:
$a=e^{\ln a}$, so $a^{x}=(e^{\ln a})^{x}=e^{x\ln a}$ **(M1)**

$5^{x}=e^{x\ln5}$, so $k=\ln5\approx1.61$ **(A1)**

This is why every exponential function is a horizontal stretch of $y=e^{x}$.

prompt:
Let $g(x)=\ln(x-2)$.

**(a)** Write down the domain of $g$. **[1]**

**(b)** Write down the equation of the vertical asymptote. **[1]**

**(c)** Find the $x$-intercept. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $x>2$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $x=2$ **(A1)**

**(c)** $\ln(x-2)=0\Rightarrow x-2=1\Rightarrow x=3$, so $(3,0)$ **(A1)**

$y=\ln(x-2)$ is $y=\ln x$ translated 2 units right; it is the inverse of $y=e^{x}+2$.
